Escalated to full path. revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire's Law No. 2013-450 on the protection of personal data requires prior declaration to, or authorisation from, the telecoms/ICT regulator ARTCI before personal data may be transferred outside the country, effectively requiring that personal data be stored and processed domestically absent regulatory approval. ARTCI, the independent authority responsible for enforcement, can issue formal notices, suspend processing authorisations and impose financial penalties for non-compliance. The requirement applies broadly to personal and sensitive data, including biometric and health data, rather than being confined to a single sector, though no separate, explicit multi-category localisation regime (e.g. covering financial or critical-infrastructure data specifically) has been enacted.

revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire's tech startup ecosystem is at an early but growing stage, concentrated in Abidjan and centred on fintech, agritech, e-commerce, logistics and edtech. Annual startup funding remains modest (estimated below US$100 million, a small share of the more than US$1 billion raised annually in more mature ecosystems such as Nigeria), dominated at seed and pre-seed stage by international investors and development finance institutions, with domestic venture capital still limited. Partech's 2025 Africa report records episodic but growing debt-funding activity in the country (around US$11 million, up 307% year-on-year). The state-backed CDC-CI Capital fund has become the most active domestic investor, making regular seed-stage grants and equity/convertible investments (including in Djamo, Julaya, ADES and Flot), and the government launched a CFA450 billion (c. US$800 million) fund in 2025 intended to further catalyse the sector.

A dedicated 2018 GSMA qualitative study of Côte d'Ivoire and Tanzania found that women face greater barriers to mobile internet adoption than men, driven mainly by social norms, lower awareness of internet use cases, affordability of smartphones and lower digital literacy, rather than explicit restrictions on access. Côte d'Ivoire has not been included among GSMA's core surveyed countries in the more recent 2022-2025 Mobile Gender Gap Reports, so no more current country-specific figure is available; the Sub-Saharan Africa regional gender gap stood at 29% in 2024.
